title: HELIX Terminology: GL Transaction Type
description: Types of general ledger journal entries in higher education financial systems.

codes.definition: Standard journal entry created by accounting staff to record transactions not captured by subsidiary systems (payroll, AP, AR). Requires balancing debits and credits with supporting documentation.
Automatic journal entry generated by a subsidiary system (payroll, accounts payable, billing, grants). Posted through batch or real-time integration. Represents the majority of GL activity.
Entry to correct an error, reclassify an expense, or adjust an estimate. Requires explanation/justification and typically additional approval. Common at month-end and year-end.
Entry to recognize revenue earned or expenses incurred but not yet recorded in cash basis. Examples: unbilled grant revenue, accrued payroll, accrued vacation liability. Required for GAAP compliance.
Entry that exactly reverses a previous entry, typically an accrual from the prior period. May be automatic (auto-reverse flag) or manual. Posted at the start of the new period.
Year-end entry to close revenue and expenditure accounts to fund balance. In fund accounting, closes each fund separately. Prepares the ledger for the new fiscal year.

Entry to move amounts between chartfield combinations (accounts, departments, funds, programs) without changing the net financial position. Common for correcting coding errors or reallocating shared costs.

Entry to eliminate intra-entity transactions in consolidated financial statements. Used when the institution has component units (foundations, hospital, research corporations) that must be consolidated per GASB standards.
Non-monetary entry recording statistical data (headcount, square footage, FTE) in the ledger for allocation and reporting purposes. Does not affect financial balances.

Entry to record the original budget, budget modifications, or encumbrances. In commitment control systems (PeopleSoft), budget entries establish spending authority against which transactions are checked.

Entry to reserve budget for a committed future expenditure (purchase order, contract, salary commitment). Reduces available budget without recording an actual expense. Liquidated when the actual expense posts.
